chunks: Hammad ibn ʿIsa narrated from Ribʿi ibn ʿAbdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man appoints someone as his executor while that person is absent, then he does not have the right to reject his bequest. And if he appoints him while he is in the town, then he has the choice: if he wishes he accepts, and if he wishes he does not accept.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed someone through a will or testamentary instruction
key_terms.بِالْبَلَدِ: present in the town or locality
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the legal option to choose
key_terms.غَائِبٌ: absent from the place at the time of appointment

ai.seo_question: Can a person refuse to act as executor of a will in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about accepting or refusing an appointment as executor of a will. If the appointment is made while the person is absent, he may not reject it, but if it is made while he is present in the town, he has the option to accept or decline.
